Paleomagnetic constraints for North China in Rodinia
New geochronologic and paleomagnetic results from early
Neoproterozoic mafic sills and late Mesoproterozoic to early
Neoproterozoic successions in the eastern North China Craton,
and implications for the reconstruction of Rodinia
Hanqing Zhao, Shihong Zhang†, Jikai Ding, Linxi Chang, Qiang Ren, Haiyan Li, Tianshui Yang, and Huaichun Wu
State Key Laboratory of Biogeology and Environmental Geology, China University of Geosciences, Beijing 100083, China

A B the section C; while 17 samples from two sites
were collected from the upper part of the Lower
Member in the section D (Figs. 4A and 6C).
Huainan Region
The Huainan region is situated on the south
bank of the Huai River drainage in the north-
ern Anhui Province, southeastern part of the
NCC (Fig. 1B). The late Mesoproterozoic to
Neoproterozoic successions are sporadically
C D
exposed in the Huainan region, and are divided
into the Huainan Gp, Feishui Gp, and Feng-
tai Fm (Figs. 4C and 5D). The Huainan Gp is
subdivided into three formations (in ascending
order, the Caodian, Bagongshan, and Liulao-
bei formations), while the Feishui Gp consists
of the Shouxian, Jiuliuqiao, and Sidingshan
formations. This succession unconformably
overlies the metamorphic rocks of the Paleopro-
terozoic Fengyang Gp, and is unconformably
E F
overlain by the Fengtai diamictite or the Cam-
brian Houjiashan Fm (Wang et al., 1984; Sun
et al., 1986; ABGMR, 1987; Dong et al., 2008).
The Liulaobei Fm is conformably overlying the
light-gray quartz sandstone of the Bagongshan

in the lower part of the Liulaobei Fm in the Huainan region. The gray arrow indicates the least-squares fit direction of the characteristic
remanent magnetization (ChRM). The directions of remanence are all in geographic coordinates. NRM—natural remanent magnetization.

netization trajectories of the representative specimens from the dolostone of the Niyuan Fm. (C) Equal area projections (after
tilt correction). The high temperature component (HTC) directions of two sites (17XZ12-15 and 17XZ11-17) of the baked dolos-
tone (dark-gray circles) from the Niyuan Fm are close to the mean direction of the sill #15XZ (dark-gray squares); while they
are obviously different from the mean direction of the Niyuan Fm in this region and the mean direction of the unbaked sites
17XZ24–17XZ28 (in light gray), suggesting that the HTC of the baked dolostone was a thermal overprint acquired during the
intrusion of the sill. Closed (open) symbols represent downward/upward magnetizations. The open star with 95% confidence
circle represents mean direction of sites 17XZ24–17XZ28. (D) The distributions of the sill #15XZ, the baked dolostone specimens
(from sites 17XZ12-15 and 17XZ11-17) and the five sites (17XZ24–17XZ28) of unbaked dolostone. Dark-gray dots represent
paleomagnetic cores of the baked specimens; light-gray elongate rectangles represent paleomagnetic sites of the unbaked dolos-
tone. Cross patterns for diabase, double slashes for baked dolostone and single slashes for unbaked dolostone.

(cid:70)(cid:68)(cid:17)(cid:20)(cid:20)(cid:19)(cid:24)(cid:48)(cid:68) (cid:70)(cid:68)(cid:17)(cid:3)(cid:20)(cid:19)(cid:27)(cid:24)(cid:3)(cid:48)(cid:68) (cid:70)(cid:68)(cid:17)(cid:3)(cid:28)(cid:23)(cid:19)(cid:3)(cid:48)(cid:68)
Figure 15. (A–B) Possible connection between the North China Craton (NCC) and Laurentia in Rodinia based on the paleomagnetic data avail-
able (in present North American coordinates). Arrows indicate the younging directions of the apparent polar wander path. The NCC and its
poles are rotated to Laurentia using Euler rotation (50.6°, 19.2°, 56.2°). Baltica and its poles are rotated to Laurentia according to the “right-
way-up” model of Laurentia–Baltica connection (Cawood and Pisarevsky, 2006) after ca. 990 Ma using Euler rotation (75.8°, –95.8°, –59.2°)
after Li et al. (2008). Aldan is rotated to Anabar using Euler rotation (60°, 115°, 25°) after Evans (2009). Anabar is rotated to Laurentia using
Euler rotation (77°, 98°, 137°) after Evans et al. (2016a). (C–E) Paleogeographic reconstructions of the NCC, Laurentia, Baltica and Siberia
in Rodinia at ca. 1105, ca. 1085, and ca. 940 Ma, respectively. (C) Circa 1105 Ma (based on the poles “NFL” and “L19” in Table 3). (D) Circa
1085 Ma (based on the poles “L9” and “BNFc” in Table 3). In Figures 15C–D, Baltica are shown in both its pre–1265 Ma position using Euler
rotation (45.0°, 7.5°, 44.9°) after Cawood et al. (2010) and post–990 Ma position, due to the opening time of the Asgard sea is not well paleomag-
netically constrained (Cawood and Pisarevsky, 2017). (E) Circa 940 Ma (based on the poles “NC930,” “WS,” and “B5” in Table 3). Absolute
longitudes for the entire assemblage are arbitrary. Cratons and their poles are matched in color. For pole symbols and more information see
the text and Table 3. BA—Baltica; SB—Siberia; SN—Sveconorwegian Belt; LA—Laurentia; YR—Yenisey Ridge.
